name: Photonic Scale Inlay
description: Introduces pangolin-derived keratin scale genes combined with morpho butterfly structural coloration to produce patches of iridescent, scale-like skin. The scales are thin, flexible, and structurally colored — they produce vivid blues, greens, and purples through light refraction rather than pigment. Common installation areas include the cheekbones, shoulders, forearms, and collarbone. Full-body coverage is possible but expensive and makes the user look genuinely non-human. The scales provide a minor defensive benefit — they're harder than normal skin — but the modification is primarily cosmetic. In the right light, a person with dragonscale catches the sun like a living gemstone. In the Shelf markets, vendors with cheekbone scales are considered fashionable and trustworthy — the modification signals someone who invests in themselves.
source_organism: Manis pentadactyla (Chinese pangolin), Morpho menelaus (blue morpho butterfly)
procedure: Dermal injection matrix with scale-growth retroviral carrier, 2 sessions
reversibility: Partially reversible; scale removal leaves textured scarring
side_effects: Scales itch intensely during growth phase
Scale edges can catch on clothing if not properly maintained
Scales may grow beyond intended boundaries over years
Dryness and flaking if not moisturized
social_perception: Glamorous and eye-catching. Popular among performers, socialites, and people who work in public-facing roles. Some traditional communities view full-body coverage as going too far.
story_hooks: A Crucible Genomics dragonscale batch produces scales with unexpected piezoelectric properties — the users generate small electrical charges when they move
A fashion mogul commissions a full-body dragonscale installation and discovers too late that the scales continue growing, requiring constant trimming to prevent full keratinization
